description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES Solicitation No. 75N99027R00002 The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Acquisition and Logistics Management (OALM), Construction, A&E, Facilities and Leasing Office (CAFLO), anticipates issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a Multiple-Award Construction Contract (MACC) to support the ongoing construction, alteration, repair, and maintenance requirements of the NIH Office of Research Facilities (ORF). The resulting contracts will be multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) construction contracts. Work will be authorized through individually issued task orders. This acquisition is anticipated to be conducted using competitive negotiated procedures under FAR Part 15. The Government intends to award multiple IDIQ construction contracts under FAR Subpart 16.5. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis. The anticipated aggregate ceiling is $3 billion over an eight-year ordering period. Individual construction requirements will be competed through task orders among eligible MACC awardees in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the resulting contracts. The solicitation and resulting contracts will include procedures for adding and removing awardees during that period (on/off ramp). The initial seed-project scope estimated construction magnitude, applicable evaluation factors, and proposal submission requirements will be provided in the solicitation. SCOPE OF WORK Work under the MACC will primarily consist of general construction and may include, but is not limited to, maintenance, repair, painting, alterations, architectural work, mechanical systems, electrical systems, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), civil work, earthwork, fencing, structural work, steel fabrication and welding, roofing, building renovations, demolition, new building construction, sustainable construction, design-bid-build, and design-build projects. Individual task orders may include one or more construction disciplines and will vary in size, scope, and complexity. All work will be performed in accordance with the requirements, specifications, drawings, and other documents applicable to each individual task order. LOCATIONS OF WORK The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Research Facilities (ORF) is the steward of NIH facilities and is responsible for the planning, design, construction, acquisition, maintenance and operation of NIH owned facilities, which include campuses in: � Bethesda, Maryland, � Frederick, Maryland, � Poolesville, Maryland, � Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, � The Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Hamilton, Montana. NAICS CODE AND SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. PSC Code: Y1JZ The corresponding small business size standard is $45 million. The NAICS code and small business size standard applicable to the initial seed project is also anticipated to be NAICS 236220 and $45 million, respectively. ACQUISITION STRATEGY AND ANTICIPATED AWARDS This acquisition will be conducted using full and open competition with reserves for eligible small business concerns. NIH anticipates awarding up to twenty (20) IDIQ contracts, consisting of: Approximately four (4) unrestricted/full-and-open awards; and Approximately sixteen (16) awards under small business reserves. The small business reserves are anticipated to include eligible concerns in the following categories: Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Small Business; Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); and Participants in the SBA 8(a) Business Development Program. The solicitation will identify the anticipated distribution of the sixteen (16) reserve awards among the applicable small business and socioeconomic categories and will establish the eligibility requirements applicable to each reserve. NIH anticipates approximately four (4) awards in each socioeconomic reserve. Offerors must meet all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the category under which they submit an offer. BONDING CAPACITY Offerors competing for an unrestricted/full-and-open award shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $100 million for a single project; and $300 million aggregate bonding capacity. Offerors competing for an award under a small business reserve shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $3 million for a single project; and $10 million aggregate bonding capacity. The solicitation will establish the specific documentation required to demonstrate bonding capacity. Performance and payment bond requirements applicable to individual construction task orders will be established in accordance with the solicitation, resulting contracts, applicable law and regulation, and the requirements of each task order. SMALL BUSINESS ELIGIBILITY AND JOINT VENTURES Offerors seeking an award under a small business reserve must satisfy all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the applicable reserve category and NAICS code. The solicitation will identify any documentation required to establish an offeror's eligibility for the applicable small business or socioeconomic category. Small business concerns intending to submit an offer as a joint venture must comply with all applicable SBA joint venture requirements, including applicable requirements governing SBA-approved Mentor-Prot�g� relationships. description: El objeto del presente contrato es la prestación de un servicio energético integral sobre las instalaciones de alumbrado público exterior del municipio de Ávila y sobre las infraestructuras eléctricas y tecnológicas vinculadas funcionalmente a dicho servicio, incluyendo su gestión energética, suministro de energía, mantenimiento preventivo y correctivo, garantía total de los elementos renovados, ejecución de inversiones con y sin ahorro energético, legalización y adecuación normativa de las instalaciones, así como la realización de actuaciones complementarias necesarias para asegurar su correcto funcionamiento, seguridad, eficiencia energética y continuidad del servicio. El objeto del contrato se circunscribe a la prestación de servicios energéticos sobre las instalaciones de alumbrado público exterior del municipio de Ávila, incluyendo sus infraestructuras eléctricas asociadas y aquellos elementos urbanos conectados a dicha red, tales como marquesinas, paradas de autobús, señalización luminosa u otros dispositivos vinculados funcionalmente al sistema de alumbrado La actuación objeto del contrato se configura como una intervención global e integrada sobre el conjunto de las instalaciones municipales, orientada a mejorar su eficiencia energética, funcionalidad, sostenibilidad ambiental y capacidad de gestión, mediante la incorporación de tecnologías eficientes, sistemas de control inteligente y herramientas digitales de monitorización y análisis. A tal efecto, el contrato comprende la realización de las inversiones necesarias, la ejecución de las obras y suministros asociados, así como la prestación de los servicios de gestión energética, mantenimiento, conservación y explotación de las instalaciones, en los términos definidos en el Pliego de Prescripciones Técnicas Particulares y en el resto de los documentos contractuales. El contrato se articula bajo la modalidad de Empresa de Servicios Energéticos (ESE), de conformidad con lo dispuesto en el artículo 19 del Real Decreto-ley 6/2010, de 9 de abril, en virtud del cual el adjudicatario asumirá la ejecución y financiación de las actuaciones necesarias, así como un determinado grado de riesgo económico, vinculando su retribución, total o parcialmente, a la consecución de ahorros energéticos derivados de la mejora de la eficiencia de las instalaciones. En este sentido, el servicio energético a prestar por el adjudicatario consistirá en un conjunto de prestaciones que incluirán, entre otras, la realización de inversiones materiales e inmateriales, la ejecución de obras, el suministro de equipos y la implantación de soluciones tecnológicas destinadas a optimizar el rendimiento de las instalaciones y reducir los costes energéticos. Dicho servicio deberá prestarse en el marco de un contrato que garantice la obtención de ahorros energéticos verificables, medibles y cuantificables, conforme a los sistemas de seguimiento y control que se establezcan. Asimismo, el contrato incorpora la implantación, mantenimiento y evolución de un sistema de gestión Smart City, que permita integrar la información relativa al funcionamiento de las instalaciones, facilitar la toma de decisiones por parte del Ayuntamiento y mejorar la eficiencia en la prestación de los servicios urbanos. La finalidad última del contrato es, por tanto, la transformación del sistema de alumbrado público y de las infraestructuras energéticas municipales en un modelo más eficiente, sostenible, digitalizado y orientado a la gestión inteligente, en línea con las estrategias de transición energética y digitalización de las Administraciones Públicas, reduciendo significativamente los consumos de energía en base a las recomendaciones establecidas en el Reglamento de Eficiencia Energética en Instalaciones de Alumbrado Exterior y dar cumplimiento a la necesidad de adecuar a la normativa de seguridad las instalaciones eléctricas.
